classes.definition: The value satisfies the documented contract, including documented optionality: NULL where the header permits NULL, an operation on a live object, non-overlapping buffers where aliasing is forbidden, a length within the buffer.
classes.implementation_guarantee: The documented behaviour, including a defined error where the operation fails. Memory safety is claimed only for paths the safety inventory covers; this register does not extend that coverage.

classes.definition: An attacker controls the value but the value still satisfies the contract: a hostile TLS record, a malformed certificate, a hostile peer public key, an attacker-chosen ciphertext or signature, a caller-chosen public geometry.
classes.implementation_guarantee: A defined refusal or a defined result. The operation must not form an invalid reference, free the wrong object, or produce a silent wrong result. Panic safety is bounded by the barriers recorded here; where a barrier is absent the class-2 guarantee is not claimed.

classes.definition: An invalid pointer, a wrong lifetime, overlapping buffers where aliasing is forbidden, a size that exceeds the buffer, NULL where the header requires non-NULL, a callback that frees the object it was invoked on, or a re-entry the external contract forbids.
classes.implementation_guarantee: NO_MEMORY_SAFETY_CLAIM. No class-3 input is ever claimed memory-safe. The practical behaviour is recorded per hazard as DEFINED_ERROR, ABORT, UB_NOT_CLAIMED_SAFE, DEFERRED_CRYPTOGRAPHIC_FAILURE or NOT_REACHABLE_FROM_CLASS_3, and whether that behaviour is a deliberate recorded divergence or an accident is stated.

input_model.class_3_rule: A hazard whose trigger set contains contract_violation may not set memory_safe_claim. The API does not enforce the contract, so the caller's obligation cannot reduce the severity; the traceability validator refuses such a hazard with TG_HAZARD_CLASS3_SAFE_CLAIM and the register validator refuses it with HR_CLASS3_SAFE_CLAIM.

families.legal: A live BIGNUM, a non-zero odd modulus where the entry point requires one, operands within the documented ranges, NULL only where the header permits it. Guaranteed: checked allocation arithmetic, refusal of an even or zero modulus where documented, fallible arithmetic returning 0.
families.class2: A hostile peer public key or an attacker-chosen ciphertext expressed as a BIGNUM, and a caller-chosen public width. Guaranteed: a defined result or refusal; the prepared-domain mismatch is refused rather than silently used.
families.class3: A freed or aliased BIGNUM, a BN_CTX used outside start/end, or a width inconsistent with the buffer. UB_NOT_CLAIMED_SAFE; partial NULL tests return 0 by authority parity, the rest is an unchecked C contract.

families.legal: A well-formed RSA object, a documented padding selector, a message no longer than the modulus, and an output buffer of RSA_size bytes. Guaranteed: blinding on by default, implicit rejection for an internal key on PKCS#1 v1.5, a defined error on failure.
families.class2: An attacker-chosen ciphertext of any length up to the modulus, a hostile signature, or a message chosen to probe padding. Guaranteed: the ciphertext is reduced and the padding check is attempted; the external-key path has no implicit rejection (HAZ-15).
families.class3: A freed RSA object, a concurrent method or key mutation, an output buffer shorter than RSA_size, or flen exceeding the input buffer. UB_NOT_CLAIMED_SAFE; the pointer contract is the authority's C contract and is not enforced.

families.legal: A live EC_KEY on a signing-capable curve, a digest, and a documented nonce_type. Guaranteed: a secure scalar for k, rejection of k == 0 and r == 0, a defined error when the deterministic arm is unavailable.
families.class2: An attacker-chosen digest or message, a hostile peer point, or a hostile signature. Guaranteed: the point is validated by the group method and the signature check is a defined result.
families.class3: A freed EC_KEY or group, a point from a different group, or a nonce buffer of the wrong size. UB_NOT_CLAIMED_SAFE.

families.legal: An initialised context, documented parameter order, lengths within the buffers, and a returned value read as documented. Guaranteed: a defined return and a defined error; the IV uniqueness obligation is the caller's and is documented, not enforced.
families.class2: A hostile ciphertext, tag or AAD, malformed parameters, or a malformed certificate handed to a decoder. Guaranteed: authentication failure or a defined error; no plaintext is claimed for a failed tag.
families.class3: A reused context where reset is required, a freed context, a lying output length, overlapping input and output where the mode forbids it, or a non-zero test of a return value that can be -1. UB_NOT_CLAIMED_SAFE or DEFERRED_CRYPTOGRAPHIC_FAILURE as recorded per hazard.

families.legal: A live BIO, the documented callback protocol, and a cb_arg that is NULL or a BIO*. Guaranteed: the callback is invoked before and after the method, and a non-positive pre-call result vetoes the operation.
families.class2: Hostile stream contents and callback behaviour supplied by an untrusted application layer. Guaranteed: a defined return; the library does not sandbox the callback.
families.class3: A cb_arg that is not a BIO*, a callback that frees the BIO it is running on, or a freed BIO. UB_NOT_CLAIMED_SAFE; the cast to BIO* and the write through it are deliberate authority parity.

families.legal: Well-formed DER, a live store context, and a verify_cb that follows the documented API. Guaranteed: bounded constructed nesting, owned chain snapshots before a callback, defined verification errors.
families.class2: A malformed or hostile certificate, a deeply nested constructed value, a very large extension, or a certificate chosen to drive policy-tree growth. Guaranteed: a defined parse or verification error; depth and length limits are applied.
families.class3: A freed context or certificate, a callback that mutates cached extension contents in place, or a certificate replaced without the ownership protocol. UB_NOT_CLAIMED_SAFE; the chain itself is protected by a snapshot, extension contents are not.

families.legal: A non-zero size where the documented branch requires it, and an installed hook that obeys the external contract. Guaranteed: a NULL return and an error on exhaustion, checked size multiplication, whole-allocation cleansing on the covered owners.
families.class2: An attacker-controlled length that reaches an allocation through a parsed field, or memory exhaustion. Guaranteed: an overflow is a checked failure, not a wrapped request; exhaustion returns NULL where the call site is fallible.
families.class3: A hook that re-enters the ERR API on the same thread, a hook that returns a misaligned pointer, or a free of a foreign pointer. UB_NOT_CLAIMED_SAFE; the same-thread ERR re-entry is additionally refused by the B34 guard, which is a recorded safety divergence.

families.legal: A fetched method used while its provider is loaded, with the documented reference-count discipline. Guaranteed: reference counting and a defined fetch failure.
families.class2: An attacker-chosen algorithm name or property query, and hostile parameters handed to a fetched implementation. Guaranteed: a defined fetch failure or a defined operation error.
families.class3: A method pointer used after the provider is unloaded or down-referenced, or a method table replaced concurrently. UB_NOT_CLAIMED_SAFE.

top_events.title: Memory corruption reachable from a class-1 or class-2 input
Denial of service by resource exhaustion
Silent wrong result in a cryptographic operation
Memory corruption reachable only from a contract-violating input (never claimed memory-safe)

hazards.title: Secret-bearing storage is freed or abandoned without cleansing
hazards.description: A secret-bearing owner releases or abandons its storage without cleansing it, so the secret survives in allocator-recycled memory.

source.quote: Release and cleansing are separate obligations: a destructor that merely frees memory is not a secret-safe destructor.

barrier.control: SecretBuf and OwnedBuf cleanse the whole allocation on the covered exit paths; the ETP-4 probe observed 85 cleanse sites.
barrier.would_close: A receipt-bound whole-allocation cleanse court at the analysis candidate, including failure and unwind paths, for every secret-bearing owner in the admitted families.

hazards.title: A secret-dependent branch, address or early exit survives optimisation
hazards.description: A branch, memory index or early exit depends on a secret value and survives optimisation, so timing reveals secret bits.

source.quote: Never claim constant-time behaviour from source inspection alone.

barrier.control: The constant-pattern ladder and the consttime division are selected on public geometry; BINSEC and the emitted-instruction audit exist as instruments.
barrier.would_close: A validated secret-dependence argument and a BINSEC verdict at the analysis candidate; both are open (OBL-T14, OBL-T16).

hazards.title: A secret-bearing allocation aborts or overflows instead of failing
hazards.description: An allocation on the secret-bearing path is infallible: exhaustion aborts the process, and an unchecked size product overflows into a too-small request.

source.quote: Infallible allocations in limbs::rem/limbs::mul; ... still plain Vecs (OBL-BN-ALLOCATOR)

barrier.control: The allocation seam is fallible and many BN sites return 0 on exhaustion; the alloc_probe failure-injection instrument is qualified.
barrier.would_close: A complete enumeration of infallible allocation sites on the secret-bearing path with a failure-injection court on each (OBL-BN-ALLOCATOR, OBL-T22).

hazards.title: An ownership boundary triggers an invalid free or a double release
hazards.description: A pointer adopted or escaped across the ownership boundary is released twice, or released by the wrong mechanism.

source.quote: A safe fn whose body can trigger an invalid free is a soundness bug even if today's call sites are correct.

barrier.control: The adoption constructors are unsafe functions with provenance contracts, and Drop is the single release of an owning handle.
barrier.would_close: A cross-caller provenance audit at the analysis candidate plus Miri over the admitted owners and their adoption sites.

hazards.title: A reference or destructor runs over a partially initialised value
hazards.description: An allocation-failure or early-return path runs a reference, an initialised read or a full destructor over a value whose initialisation invariants do not yet hold. A legal out-of-memory condition is enough to reach this state.

source.quote: No &T, &mut T, initialized read, or full destructor is permitted before the required initialization invariants hold.

barrier.control: OwnedRaw distinguishes uninitialised storage from OwnedCtx, and a destructor releases only the resources actually acquired.
barrier.would_close: A failure-injection and Miri run over every partially initialised owner at the analysis candidate.

hazards.title: An application callback re-enters and invalidates a borrow or lock
hazards.description: An application callback invoked inside an operation frees, replaces or mutates the object the operation is reading, so the operation continues with a dangling pointer or a stale borrow.

source.quote: Treat FFI callbacks and hooks as reentrancy edges.

barrier.control: v3_addr snapshots the chain and up-references each certificate before verify_cb; the BIO and allocator callback paths have no equivalent snapshot.
barrier.would_close: A per-call-site callback map with a reentrancy court for x509, BIO, EVP and allocator hooks (OBL-XCUT-CALLBACKS).

hazards.title: A secret-derived length or capability survives into a copy or allocation
hazards.description: A length, capacity or allocated width derived from a secret value reaches a copy, an allocation or an admission check, so the secret length is observable.

source.quote: Secret-length-dependent boundary copy and admission checks (the 19 length-taint sites)

barrier.control: The staging transfer reads a public width; the remaining secret-length presence test is stated rather than removed.
barrier.would_close: A public-width transfer with no secret-length branch and a timing court at the analysis candidate (OBL-T9).

hazards.title: An RSA private operation runs without blinding
hazards.description: Blinding is disabled by the application or fails to be constructed, so the private exponentiation runs with a secret-dependent pattern an observer can correlate with the message.

source.quote: The blinding is skipped for `RSA_FLAG_NO_BLINDING`

barrier.control: Blinding is on by default, and a NULL blinding aborts the operation; RSA_blinding_off and RSA_FLAG_NO_BLINDING are documented optionality.
barrier.would_close: A measured timing court at the analysis candidate with blinding enabled and disabled, plus a consumer audit of blinding disabling.

hazards.title: A fault during CRT produces a faulty signature or key recovery
hazards.description: A fault injected into one CRT half produces a result that is not congruent; the tail's check is the only defence and the fallback is itself a secret operation.

source.quote: falls back to the unblinded `d` exponentiation when the CRT answer does not check out

barrier.control: The CRT tail re-exponentiates with the public exponent and compares congruently, falling back to the raw-d exponentiation on a mismatch.
barrier.would_close: A receipt-bound fault-injection court at the analysis candidate showing the check fires and the fallback repairs, with a timing argument for the fallback.

hazards.title: A stale or mismatched Montgomery context yields a wrong-modulus result
hazards.description: A caller-supplied prepared context belongs to a different modulus or width. The authority does not validate it and silently produces a wrong answer; this crate refuses it, which is a recorded divergence.

source.quote: The authority does not validate `in_mont`; a stale context silently produces

barrier.control: BN_mod_exp_mont_consttime validates a supplied context against the operand and refuses a mismatch instead of reproducing the authority's silent wrong answer.
barrier.would_close: A differential court at the analysis candidate for prepared-domain reuse across moduli, including the cached RSA CRT context.

hazards.title: An ECDSA nonce is biased or reused
hazards.description: The signing scalar k is drawn from a weak, biased or repeated source, so two signatures reveal the private key. The RFC 6979 arm is not landed and refuses rather than silently substituting the random arm.

source.quote: The nonce's two nested loops: the inner one redraws while `k == 0`

barrier.control: k is drawn into a BN_secure_new scalar, k == 0 and r == 0 are rejected, and the deterministic arm refuses with an error rather than falling through.
barrier.would_close: A nonce-distribution and repetition court at the analysis candidate, and a recorded decision on landing RFC 6979 (D333).

hazards.title: Allocation arithmetic overflows on an attacker-controlled length
hazards.description: A count product or length sum derived from a parsed field overflows and reaches the allocator as a too-small request, or is treated as unbounded.

source.quote: The product is `checked_mul`-guarded: an overflow is the

barrier.control: OwnedBlock and OwnedBuf compute count*size with checked_mul and answer None on overflow; an over-aligned type is refused before the allocator is asked.
barrier.would_close: A fuzz court that drives parsed lengths into every allocation helper and observes the failure arm at the analysis candidate.

hazards.title: An allocator hook re-enters the error subsystem on the same thread
hazards.description: A caller-installed allocation hook calls ERR_raise or any entry point that takes the thread's error state while the allocator already holds it, forming a second mutable borrow.

source.quote: so a hook that violates the contract fails closed rather than causing UB.

barrier.control: with_state refuses a same-thread re-entry with a thread-local guard and returns the no-state outcome; this is a recorded safety divergence (B34).
barrier.would_close: A negative-control court that installs a re-entering allocator hook and observes the fail-closed outcome at the analysis candidate.

hazards.title: A verify callback mutates state the walk is reading
hazards.description: An application verify_cb releases or replaces the chain, or mutates a cached extension in place, while the validation walk still reads it.

source.quote: What cannot be guaranteed: a callback that mutates the *contents* of a live cached extension in

barrier.control: v3_addr snapshots the chain, up-references each certificate and re-reads the cached extension after a callback; in-place mutation of a cached extension is stated as unprotected.
barrier.would_close: A reentrancy court for verify_cb and an ownership model for cached extension contents (OBL-XCUT-CALLBACKS).

hazards.title: External-key PKCS#1 v1.5 decryption has no implicit rejection
hazards.description: For a key with RSA_FLAG_EXT_PKEY the KDK cannot be derived, so the selector is rewritten to the refusing check. An attacker measuring the refusal distinguishes padding validity.

source.quote: an external key does not hold the

barrier.control: None on the external-key path: implicit rejection exists only where the private exponent is held by the library.
barrier.would_close: An external-key implicit-rejection design, or a recorded consumer exclusion for every in-scope external-key PKCS#1 v1.5 decryption path (OBL-RSA-EXTKEY-ORACLE).

hazards.title: A panic at the FFI boundary leaves partially mutated state
hazards.description: A panic is caught and never unwinds into C, but the interrupted operation has already mutated the context; the caller's next operation sees the half-applied change.

source.quote: panicking FFI call is itself the defect to fix, not something this boundary

barrier.control: guard_ffi catches and never resumes, so no panic unwinds into C; it does not repair partially mutated state.
barrier.would_close: Failure-atomic mutation, explicit rollback or explicit poisoning for every stateful FFI context that can panic (OBL-PANIC-ATOMICITY, OBL-XCUT-PANIC).

hazards.title: A hostile certificate exhausts stack, time or memory
hazards.description: A constructed ASN.1 value nested to the limit, or an extension whose parsed representation grows with the input, consumes resources in proportion to attacker-chosen input.

source.quote: `ASN1_MAX_CONSTRUCTED_NEST` — how deeply a constructed value may nest.

barrier.control: ASN1_MAX_CONSTRUCTED_NEST (30), ASN1_GEN_SEQ_MAX_DEPTH and MAX_STRING_NEST bound constructed nesting; length checks use checked arithmetic.
barrier.would_close: A hostile-certificate fuzz court that measures peak depth, time and memory at the analysis candidate.

hazards.title: A consumer confuses a verification error with a valid signature
hazards.description: EVP_DigestVerifyFinal answers 0 for an invalid signature and -1 for an error. A consumer that tests non-zero as success accepts the error as a valid signature; the C ABI cannot force the distinction.

source.quote: with 0** — where `EVP_DigestVerify` answers `-1` for the same state

barrier.control: The return contract is documented (1 valid, 0 invalid, -1 error); the C ABI provides no type that forces a consumer to test it exactly.
barrier.would_close: A consumer audit that every in-scope verification call site tests exactly 1 (OBL-VERIFY-RETURN-POLARITY).

hazards.title: A shared object is freed or has its method changed under a live operation
hazards.description: The cached Montgomery slot and the method table are read without an enforced lifetime: another thread may free the enclosing object or change its method while the operation uses the published context.

source.quote: This function **never frees or replaces a published context**. The context is

barrier.control: Publication is a Release store and the slot fast path an Acquire load; the enclosing object's exclusive-access precondition is documented but not enforced.
barrier.would_close: A concurrency court that exercises method change and object free against a live operation, and a scoped caller precondition (OBL-MECH-RUNTIME-CONCURRENCY).

hazards.title: A BIO callback writes through a cb_arg that is not a BIO
hazards.description: BIO_debug_callback_ex treats cb_arg as char* and casts it to BIO*; a caller that sets a non-BIO argument gets the authority's behaviour, a write into whatever the pointer addresses.

source.quote: non-BIO argument gets the authority's behaviour (a write into whatever the

barrier.control: None: cb_arg is typed char* in the header and cast to BIO*; the authority writes through whatever the pointer addresses and this is reproduced deliberately.
barrier.would_close: A typed callback-argument contract, or an explicit refusal of a non-BIO cb_arg recorded as a safety divergence (OBL-XCUT-CALLBACKS).

assumptions.statement: The adversary can measure the operation's timing at the granularity the blinding or constant-time defence targets.
The DRBG state or its entropy source can be compromised (THR-08); no library-level countermeasure compensates for a fully known DRBG state.
The adversary observes the signatures a signer produces, including two signatures under a repeated or biased nonce.
A local adversary can induce a fault in one CRT half while the exponentiation runs.
An in-scope consumer tests the verification return value as non-zero rather than exactly 1.
The attacker submits ciphertexts of its choice to a PKCS#1 v1.5 decryption oracle and observes the success or failure.
The AEAD caller supplies a unique IV per key; the library documents this obligation and does not enforce it.
The adversary observes the ciphertexts and tags the application produces.
The attacker supplies the certificate bytes a consumer parses or verifies.
The library applies no process-wide cap on a single request's allocation size; the deployment supplies the memory bound.
A caller can supply or cache a prepared Montgomery context across a modulus change.
The public-exponent congruence check is the only cross-check on a CRT result before it is returned.
A class-2 input reaches a panic only through an internal defect; the register does not certify that no such defect exists.
The caller chooses the modulus and exponent sizes, so the ladder width and the operation count are attacker-influenced public geometry.
A consumer that tests a verification result for success uses exactly the documented success value.
No independent implementation re-derives these results at the analysis candidate; the authority differential is the only oracle.

fault_trees.description: A private key is disclosed through a nonce, a timing channel, residual secret storage or a compromised DRBG.
fault_trees.diagram: TE-1 = OR( AND(HAZ-08 blinding skipped, ASM-TIMING-OBSERVER), AND(HAZ-11 nonce biased/reused, ASM-SIGNATURES-OBSERVED), AND(HAZ-02 secret branch, ASM-TIMING-OBSERVER), HAZ-01 un-cleansed storage, ASM-DRBG-COMPROMISE )

nodes.statement: Blinding is skipped when RSA_FLAG_NO_BLINDING is set or RSA_blinding_off was called.
The signing scalar k comes from ossl_bn_priv_rand_range_fixed_top, or from the DSA-style nonce derived from the private key and digest.
The exponentiation ladder and the reduction kernels are the constant-pattern code in bn, but the branch audit has no verdict at the candidate.
A secret-bearing owner frees storage after the last use without a whole-allocation cleanse.
A fully compromised DRBG state discloses the key directly; the register records this as an assumption rather than a barrier.
The adversary measures timing at the granularity the defence targets.
The adversary obtains signatures produced under the biased or repeated nonce.

fault_trees.description: A signature is forged, or a verification failure is read as success.
fault_trees.diagram: TE-2 = OR( AND(HAZ-09 CRT fault, ASM-FAULT-INJECTION), AND(HAZ-18 return-value confusion, ASM-CONSUMER-NONZERO-TEST) )

nodes.statement: A fault in one CRT half yields a non-congruent result; the tail's check and the raw-d fallback are the only defence.
EVP_DigestVerifyFinal returns 0 for invalid and -1 for error; the ABI cannot force a consumer to test exactly 1.
A local adversary can inject a fault during the CRT exponentiations.
The consumer tests the verification return value as non-zero rather than exactly 1.

fault_trees.description: Plaintext or the confidentiality key is disclosed through a padding oracle, residual storage, or AEAD nonce reuse.
fault_trees.diagram: TE-3 = OR( AND(HAZ-15 external-key oracle, ASM-ATTACKER-CHOSEN-CIPHERTEXT), HAZ-01 un-cleansed storage, AND(GCM encrypt without a uniqueness check, ASM-AEAD-NONCE-REUSE, ASM-ATTACKER-OBSERVES-CIPHERTEXTS) )

nodes.statement: An external key substitutes RSA_PKCS1_NO_IMPLICIT_REJECT_PADDING and takes the refusing padding check, so refusal is observable.
Plaintext or key material survives in freed storage without a whole-allocation cleanse.
The GCM engine encrypts with the caller's IV and does not check uniqueness.
The attacker submits ciphertexts of its choice and observes success or failure.
The caller reuses an IV under one key.
The adversary observes the ciphertexts and tags produced under the reused nonce.

fault_trees.description: Memory corruption reached with a legal or adversarial-but-contract-valid input. Class-3-only hazards are excluded from this top event by construction.
fault_trees.diagram: TE-4 = OR( HAZ-05 partial initialisation on OOM, HAZ-12 allocation-arithmetic overflow, HAZ-06 callback invalidates a legal-view, AND(HAZ-16 panic caught but state half-applied, ASM-PANIC-REACHABLE-FROM-CLASS2) )

nodes.statement: An allocation failure mid-construction leaves a partially initialised owner that a reference or full destructor then touches.
A parsed count product reaches an allocation helper without checked arithmetic.
A documented callback replaces the chain or an extension the walk is reading; only the chain is snapshotted.
A caught panic leaves the context partially mutated; guard_ffi does not roll back or poison.
A class-2 input reaches a panic through an internal defect; no such defect is certified absent.

fault_trees.description: Resource exhaustion from an unbounded allocation, hostile nesting, or a caller-chosen public geometry.
fault_trees.diagram: TE-5 = OR( AND(HAZ-03 infallible allocation aborts, ASM-UNBOUNDED-REQUEST), AND(HAZ-17 hostile nesting, ASM-CALLER-CONTROLLED-CERTIFICATE), AND(ladder width from caller geometry, ASM-CALLER-CONTROLS-PUBLIC-GEOMETRY) )

nodes.statement: An infallible allocation on the BN path aborts the process on exhaustion.
A constructed value nested to the depth cap consumes a stack frame per level.
The ladder width and operation count follow the caller-supplied modulus and exponent size.
The library applies no process-wide request cap; the deployment supplies the bound.
The attacker supplies the certificate bytes.
The caller chooses the public geometry.

fault_trees.description: A cryptographic operation returns a wrong result instead of failing.
fault_trees.diagram: TE-6 = OR( AND(HAZ-10 stale Montgomery context, ASM-PREPARED-DOMAIN-REUSED), AND(HAZ-09 CRT result trusted after the fallback, ASM-CRT-CHECK-IS-THE-ONLY-ORACLE) )

nodes.statement: A supplied Montgomery context is used without a modulus match in the authority; this crate refuses it instead.
The CRT result is repaired by a raw-d fallback whose own result is returned without a second congruence check.
A caller reuses or caches a prepared context across a modulus change.
The public-exponent check is the only cross-check on the CRT result.

fault_trees.description: A secret-dependent operation loses its constant-time or fixed-pattern property.
fault_trees.diagram: TE-7 = OR( AND(HAZ-02 secret branch, ASM-TIMING-OBSERVER), AND(HAZ-07 secret length, ASM-TIMING-OBSERVER), AND(HAZ-08 blinding skipped, ASM-TIMING-OBSERVER), AND(HAZ-11 nonce source, ASM-SIGNATURES-OBSERVED) )

nodes.statement: A secret-dependent branch or index survives optimisation in the ladder, inversion or division.
A secret-derived length reaches a copy or an allocation and is observable.
The private exponentiation runs unblinded when the caller disables blinding.
The nonce source's output distribution is observable through the signatures it produces.
The adversary measures timing at the defence's granularity.
The adversary obtains the signatures.

fault_trees.description: Memory corruption reachable only when the caller violates the documented contract. This tree is deliberately disjoint from TE-4: nothing here is reachable from a legal or adversarial-but-contract-valid input, and nothing here is claimed memory-safe.
fault_trees.diagram: TE-8 = OR( HAZ-04 invalid free/double release, HAZ-13 allocator-hook re-entry, HAZ-14 verify_cb mutates a cached extension, HAZ-19 object freed or method changed under an operation, HAZ-20 BIO cb_arg is not a BIO )

nodes.statement: A raw pointer is adopted with the wrong provenance or released twice.
An installed allocation hook re-enters the ERR API on the same thread.
verify_cb mutates the contents of a cached extension in place while the walk reads it.
The enclosing object is freed or its method changed while a published Montgomery slot is in use.
cb_arg is not a BIO* and the callback writes through it.

fmea.failure_mode: Allocation fails on an installed or default allocator.
fmea.local_effect: NULL return and an error raised.
fmea.control: Every caller on the fallible seam tests the NULL return and takes its error path.
fmea.residual: The infallible BN Vec sites take the abort path instead (OBL-BN-ALLOCATOR).

fmea.failure_mode: count*size overflows size_t.
fmea.local_effect: The product is checked and the call answers NULL instead of a wrapped request.
fmea.control: ossl_size_mul and OwnedBlock/OwnedBuf checked_mul guards.
fmea.residual: No fuzz court drives parsed lengths through every helper.

fmea.failure_mode: Installed hook re-enters ERR on the same thread.
fmea.local_effect: A second mutable borrow of ERR_STATE would be formed without the guard.
fmea.control: with_state refuses a same-thread re-entry with a thread-local guard; a recorded safety divergence (B34).
fmea.residual: No negative-control court at the candidate installs a re-entering hook.

fmea.failure_mode: The write is elided because the storage is about to be freed.
fmea.local_effect: Secret residue survives in recycled memory.
fmea.control: The value barrier in the cleanse path prevents the elision.
fmea.residual: No receipt binds the emitted code at the analysis candidate.

fmea.failure_mode: Scratch temporaries are released without cleansing.
fmea.local_effect: Nonce and scalar intermediates remain in the pool.
fmea.control: None recorded.
fmea.residual: OBL-T12-RESIDUAL remains open.

fmea.failure_mode: A stale or mismatched context is supplied for the operand.
fmea.local_effect: The authority's silent wrong answer would be reproduced if the check were absent.
fmea.control: context_matches validates modulus, word and backend; a mismatch raises and returns 0.
fmea.residual: The refusal has no authority coordinate; no differential court exercises reuse.

fmea.failure_mode: The enclosing object is freed or its method changed while the context is in use.
fmea.local_effect: The published context is read after its owner released it.
fmea.control: Atomic Acquire/Release publication; the object's exclusive-access precondition is documented.
fmea.residual: The precondition is not enforced; OBL-MECH-RUNTIME-CONCURRENCY is open.

fmea.failure_mode: Division runs a variable-time path on a secret operand.
fmea.local_effect: Quotient bits are observable in timing.
fmea.control: BN_FLG_CONSTTIME routes a flagged call to div_rem_ct_fallible.
fmea.residual: The routing is not measured at the candidate; row T28 records the mechanism only.

fmea.failure_mode: A Vec allocation on the secret-bearing path is infallible.
fmea.local_effect: Exhaustion aborts the process.
fmea.control: Partially fallible wrappers; OBL-BN-ALLOCATOR tracks the remaining sites.
fmea.residual: One allocation per limb operation remains (row T29).

fmea.failure_mode: A secret-dependent branch survives optimisation.
fmea.local_effect: Timing reveals exponent bits.
fmea.control: BINSEC -checkct and binary_branch_audit are qualified instruments.
fmea.residual: BINSEC returns unknown on the ladder; OBL-T16-RESIDUAL.

fmea.failure_mode: A secret-length presence or bounds test branches.
fmea.local_effect: The secret's length is observable.
fmea.control: The transfer reads a public width; the remaining secret-length test is stated.
fmea.residual: OBL-T9-RESIDUAL remains open.

fmea.failure_mode: The caller disables blinding.
fmea.local_effect: The private exponentiation runs with a message-correlated pattern.
fmea.control: Blinding is on by default; disabling it is documented optionality.
fmea.residual: No timing court distinguishes the blinding-disabled path.

fmea.failure_mode: No blinding can be constructed for the key.
fmea.local_effect: The operation raises and returns failure; it does not proceed unblinded.
fmea.control: A NULL blinding takes the error path and breaks the operation.
fmea.residual: The error path is source-only; no failure-injection receipt.

fmea.failure_mode: A fault makes the CRT result non-congruent.
fmea.local_effect: The result is repaired by the raw-d fallback, or an unpredicted value is returned if the check itself is wrong.
fmea.control: Re-exponentiation with e and a congruence comparison, then the fallback.
fmea.residual: A unit test exercises the fallback; no receipt-bound fault court exists.

fmea.failure_mode: RSA_FLAG_EXT_PKEY forces the refusing PKCS#1 v1.5 check.
fmea.local_effect: The refusal is observable; implicit rejection is unavailable.
fmea.control: None on this path.
fmea.residual: OBL-RSA-EXTKEY-ORACLE is open and blocks the b85c claim.

fmea.failure_mode: The blinding factor is released with BN_free rather than cleansed.
fmea.local_effect: The blinding factor survives in freed storage.
fmea.control: None recorded.
fmea.residual: OBL-T11-RESIDUAL remains open.

fmea.failure_mode: Recombination reads p/q, zero limbs and carries.
fmea.local_effect: Factors and their shape are observable in timing.
fmea.control: None recorded.
fmea.residual: OBL-T6-RESIDUAL remains open.

fmea.failure_mode: k is biased or repeated by the DRBG or the nonce derivation.
fmea.local_effect: Two signatures reveal the private key.
fmea.control: BN_secure_new scalar, zero rejection, and the deterministic arm refuses instead of substituting.
fmea.residual: No nonce-distribution court and no RFC 6979 decision at the candidate.

fmea.failure_mode: A consumer treats -1 (error) as a valid result.
fmea.local_effect: An unverified signature is accepted.
fmea.control: The documented return contract; the ABI cannot enforce it.
fmea.residual: No consumer audit of return-value tests (OBL-VERIFY-RETURN-POLARITY).

fmea.failure_mode: A fetched method is used after the provider is unloaded.
fmea.local_effect: The method table pointer is dangling.
fmea.control: Provider and method reference counts.
fmea.residual: No unload-race court at the candidate.

fmea.failure_mode: No implementation matches the name and properties.
fmea.local_effect: A defined NULL result and a fetch error.
fmea.control: A defined fetch failure.
fmea.residual: No receipt for the property-query failure matrix.

fmea.failure_mode: The caller reuses an IV under one key.
fmea.local_effect: The authentication key and plaintext are recoverable.
fmea.control: None: uniqueness is a documented caller obligation and is not enforced.
fmea.residual: Recorded as an assumption, not a barrier.

fmea.failure_mode: cb_arg is not a BIO*, and the callback writes through it.
fmea.local_effect: A write to an arbitrary address.
fmea.control: None: the cast is deliberate authority parity.
fmea.residual: Class-3 only; never claimed memory-safe.

fmea.failure_mode: The callback frees the BIO the operation is running on.
fmea.local_effect: The method continues with a dangling BIO.
fmea.control: None: no snapshot or up-ref around the BIO callback path.
fmea.residual: Class-2 application behaviour is not sandboxed.

fmea.failure_mode: verify_cb releases or replaces the chain.
fmea.local_effect: The walk would read a freed stack or certificate.
fmea.control: ChainSnapshot duplicates the stack and up-references every certificate.
fmea.residual: No reentrancy court exercises the snapshot.

fmea.failure_mode: verify_cb mutates a cached extension in place.
fmea.local_effect: Elements already contributed to the child stack change under the walk.
fmea.control: None; the module states the residual explicitly.
fmea.residual: IPAddressFamily has no shared-ownership handle.

fmea.failure_mode: A constructed value nests to the depth cap or an extension expands with the input.
fmea.local_effect: High stack or time consumption relative to the input length.
fmea.control: MAX_CONSTRUCTED_NEST (30), ASN1_GEN_SEQ_MAX_DEPTH and MAX_STRING_NEST.
fmea.residual: No hostile-certificate resource measurement at the candidate.

fmea.failure_mode: An allocation failure mid-construction publishes a partial tree.
fmea.local_effect: A destructor or a reference touches an uninitialised member.
fmea.control: OwnedTree/OwnedLevels release only acquired members; failure-injection refuses the first node request.
fmea.residual: The failure-injection is a unit test, not a receipt at the candidate.

fmea.failure_mode: A panic interrupts a stateful operation.
fmea.local_effect: The context is left half-mutated; the documented failure value is returned.
fmea.control: Non-unwinding only; no rollback or poison.
fmea.residual: Failure-atomicity is absent (OBL-PANIC-ATOMICITY, OBL-XCUT-PANIC).

fmea.failure_mode: A raw pointer is adopted with the wrong allocator, extent or release mechanism.
fmea.local_effect: A double release, an invalid free or a leak.
fmea.control: Adoption constructors are unsafe with provenance contracts; Drop is the single release.
fmea.residual: No cross-caller provenance audit or Miri run at the candidate (OBL-XCUT-ALIASING).

nodes.description: OpenSSL-compatible C ABI entry points in libcrypto.
EVP dispatch and provider fetch/method-store layer.
BN, RSA, EC and cipher kernels.
ASN.1 parse and X.509 verification walk.
libc allocator, OS entropy and the process boundary.
Application callbacks: verify_cb, BIO callbacks, allocator hooks, ex_data.

edges.action: parse a certificate and run the verification walk
allocate a policy tree or an extension copy
draw a nonce, blinding factor or key
register a callback and its argument
re-enter the library from a callback
return a status code and the ERR queue

ucas.control_action: Publish an owning handle whose lifetime is the caller's.
ucas.context: Another thread frees the enclosing object or changes its method while an operation holds the handle.
ucas.loss: Use after free or a data race.
ucas.barrier: Atomic slot publication only; the exclusive-access precondition is not enforced.

ucas.control_action: Invoke an application callback while an operation holds a reference into a stack or an extension.
ucas.context: The callback releases, replaces or mutates that object, which the documented API permits.
ucas.barrier: Chain snapshot for verify_cb; no barrier for BIO and no protection for extension contents.

ucas.control_action: Call the installed allocation hook while ERR holds the thread's error state.
ucas.context: The hook calls ERR_raise or ERR_get_error on the same thread, contrary to the external contract.
ucas.loss: A second mutable borrow of ERR_STATE.
ucas.barrier: B34 thread-local re-entry guard fails closed (recorded safety divergence).

ucas.control_action: Run the private exponentiation with blinding disabled.
ucas.context: The application called RSA_blinding_off or set RSA_FLAG_NO_BLINDING, or blinding construction failed.
ucas.loss: A timing channel on the private exponent.
ucas.barrier: Blinding is on by default; disabling is not measured.

ucas.control_action: Return the PKCS#1 v1.5 padding verdict for an external key.
ucas.context: The key has RSA_FLAG_EXT_PKEY and the caller requested PKCS#1 padding.
ucas.loss: A padding oracle on the private key.

ucas.control_action: Return the result of a prepared-domain operation.
ucas.context: The supplied context belongs to a different modulus and the check is bypassed or absent.
ucas.barrier: context_matches refuses a mismatch in this crate.

ucas.context: A fault occurs in one CRT half.
ucas.loss: A faulty signature or factor recovery.
ucas.barrier: Congruence check and raw-d fallback; no fault court.

ucas.control_action: Catch a panic and return the documented failure value.
ucas.context: The interrupted operation had already mutated a stateful context.
ucas.loss: A half-applied state reused by the next call.
ucas.barrier: Non-unwinding only; no rollback or poison.

ucas.context: A consumer tests the result as non-zero instead of exactly 1.
ucas.barrier: The documented contract; the ABI cannot enforce it.

ucas.control_action: Write the debug trace through cb_arg.
ucas.context: The application set cb_arg to a pointer that is not a BIO*.
ucas.loss: A write through an arbitrary pointer.

ucas.control_action: Abort the process when an infallible allocation fails.
ucas.context: The secret-bearing BN path allocates through Vec while memory is exhausted.
ucas.loss: Denial of service for every connection in the process.

ucas.control_action: Continue the validation walk after a callback.
ucas.context: The callback mutated a cached extension in place.
ucas.loss: Stale elements already contributed to the child stack.
ucas.barrier: None for extension contents; the module states the residual.

attack_graphs.title: Biased or reused ECDSA nonce to private-key recovery
preconditions: The signer uses the DSA-style nonce or a DRBG whose output is biased or repeated.
steps: Sign two messages whose nonces are equal or related.
Recover k from the two signature equations.
Recover the private scalar from k and one signature.
attack_graphs.barrier: BN_secure_new for k, rejection of k == 0 and r == 0, and refusal of the deterministic arm instead of a silent fallback.
attack_graphs.residual: No nonce-distribution or repetition court at the analysis candidate, and D333 leaves RFC 6979 unlanded.

attack_graphs.title: Blinding removal or blinding failure to a timing attack
preconditions: The application disables blinding or blinding construction fails.
The adversary measures the private operation.
steps: Force the no-blinding path.
Collect timings for chosen messages.
Correlate the pattern with the private exponent.
attack_graphs.barrier: Blinding is on by default and a NULL blinding aborts the operation.
attack_graphs.residual: Disabling blinding is documented optionality with no measured consequence at the candidate.

attack_graphs.title: CRT fault to a faulty signature and factor recovery
preconditions: The adversary can inject a fault in one CRT half.
The library returns a signature without a congruence check.
steps: Induce a fault during one per-prime exponentiation.
Obtain the faulty signature.
Compute gcd of the faulty and correct signatures to recover a factor.
attack_graphs.barrier: Re-exponentiation with the public exponent, a congruence comparison, and the raw-d fallback.
attack_graphs.residual: A unit test exercises the fallback; no receipt-bound fault-injection court exists at the candidate.

attack_graphs.title: Allocation failure mid-operation to a partial or inconsistent state
preconditions: The caller installs a failing allocator or the process is exhausted.
An operation has already acquired some resources.
steps: Fail the Nth allocation inside a construction or a private operation.
The call returns its documented failure value.
A destructor or the next call touches the partially initialised state.
attack_graphs.barrier: The fallible allocation seam, OwnedBuf/OwnedTree release-only-acquired destructors, and error returns before publication.
attack_graphs.residual: Infallible BN Vec allocations and the absence of a failure-injection court at the candidate (OBL-BN-ALLOCATOR, OBL-T22).

attack_graphs.title: A stale cached Montgomery context to a wrong-modulus result
preconditions: A caller reuses or shares a prepared context across a modulus change.
The operation trusts the supplied context.
steps: Supply a context prepared for modulus m1 to an operation on m2.
The authority computes with the wrong parameters and returns a plausible value.
The caller uses the wrong result.
attack_graphs.barrier: context_matches compares modulus, word and backend, and refuse_context raises instead of computing.
attack_graphs.residual: The refusal has no authority coordinate and no differential court for reuse at the candidate.

attack_graphs.title: A callback re-enters and mutates state under an operation
preconditions: The application registered a callback through a documented entry point.
The callback frees or replaces the object the operation is reading.
steps: The operation invokes the callback.
The callback frees the chain, replaces the BIO or mutates a cached extension.
The operation continues with the stale pointer or borrow.
attack_graphs.barrier: ChainSnapshot and per-certificate up-refs for x509; the B34 guard for same-thread ERR re-entry; no barrier for BIO cb_arg or extension contents.
attack_graphs.residual: OBL-XCUT-CALLBACKS remains NOT_ESTABLISHED; in-place extension mutation is explicitly unprotected.

attack_graphs.title: External-key PKCS#1 v1.5 padding oracle to plaintext disclosure
preconditions: A private key is held externally (RSA_FLAG_EXT_PKEY).
The application decrypts attacker-supplied PKCS#1 v1.5 ciphertexts and reports success or failure.
steps: Submit a modified ciphertext.
Observe whether the padding check refuses.
Iterate to recover the plaintext (Bleichenbacher/ROBOT).
attack_graphs.barrier: None on the external-key path; implicit rejection exists only for a key whose private exponent the library holds.
attack_graphs.residual: OBL-RSA-EXTKEY-ORACLE is open and blocks the b85c graduation.

non_claims: This register does not establish that any listed hazard is unreachable. It records a scope, a trigger classification and a barrier state.
A barrier recorded as CLAIMED_NO_EVIDENCE is not a discharged control; a hazard recorded as BARRIER_ABSENT is not mitigated.
No class-3 input is claimed memory-safe, and no caller obligation is used to reduce a hazard's severity.
No constant-time claim is made from source inspection; ASM-TIMING-OBSERVER is an assumption the register records, not a measurement.
The register does not replace the T1 traceability graph. It projects its hazards into that graph and does not fork a second model.
Population completeness is UNKNOWN: no frozen expected-hazard manifest exists, so the register cannot prove it lists every hazard in the admitted surfaces.
The register does not adjudicate a release claim. A hazard that reaches a claim adds an obligation; it does not decide the claim.
